def-qc-dyadic-cyclotomic-ring:
## Definition

Set $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$, $K=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $O=\mathbb Z[\omega]$, and
$D=O[1/2]=\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$. The relation $\omega^4=-1$ reduces every
element of $O$ to four integer coefficients in the power basis
$1,\omega,\omega^2,\omega^3$. The canonical dyadic encoding of a nonzero
$z\in D$ is

$$z=(a_0+a_1\omega+a_2\omega^2+a_3\omega^3)/2^r,$$

where $r\ge0$ is least and, if $r>0$, the four integers are not all even.
Zero is encoded with $r=0$ and all four coefficients zero. Arithmetic is exact:
multiply polynomials, reduce with $\omega^4=-1$, combine denominators, and
remove the common power of $2$ from the coefficients. The integral-basis
supplier [[thm-cyclotomic-ring-of-integers]] and the proof of
[[lem-qc-dyadic-coefficient-encoding]] justify existence and uniqueness.
lem-qc-modular-square-root-expected-poly:
## Statement

Given a prime integer $p$ and an integer $a$, there is an exact randomized algorithm that returns a square root of $a$ modulo $p$ or correctly reports that none exists. With ordinary binary integers, schoolbook arithmetic and independent unbiased random bits, its expected bit cost is polynomial in the input length; after reducing $a$ modulo $p$, it is $O((1+\log p)^4)$. Every returned answer is correct, and the algorithm terminates with probability one. The input promise that $p$ is prime is not a primality test.
def-qc-cyclotomic-bullet-automorphism:
## Definition

Let $K=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, where $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$. The class $[5]_8$ is a
unit modulo $8$, so the cyclotomic Galois group supplier
[[cor-the-galois-group-of-a-rational-cyclotomic-field]] gives the unique
$\mathbb Q$-automorphism $\bullet$ with
$\omega^\bullet=\omega^5=-\omega$. It fixes $i=\omega^2$ and sends
$\sqrt2=\omega-\omega^3$ to $-\sqrt2$. Complex conjugation and $\bullet$
commute, as is checked on the generator $\omega$. The four embeddings of $K$
are the identity, complex conjugation, $\bullet$, and their composite,
because the Galois group consists of the four maps $\omega\mapsto\omega^j$
for $j=1,3,5,7$. Since $\bullet$ fixes $1/2$ and maps $\omega$ into
$\mathbb Z[\omega]$, it preserves $D=\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$.

This is the nontrivial real-conjugation embedding used in the scaled-grid
conditions; it is distinct from complex conjugation.
lem-qc-dyadic-coefficient-encoding:
## Statement

Every $z\in D$ has exactly one canonical dyadic encoding specified in
[[def-qc-dyadic-cyclotomic-ring]].
lem-qc-sqrt-two-divisibility-criterion:
## Statement

For $x=a+b\omega+c\omega^2+d\omega^3\in O$, multiplication by
$\sqrt2=\omega-\omega^3$ has coefficient vector
$(b-d,a+c,b+d,c-a)$. Consequently $\sqrt2$ divides $x$ in $O$ exactly when
$a\equiv c$ and $b\equiv d\pmod2$. Also,

$$x\bar x=P+\sqrt2Q,\qquad P=a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2,\quad Q=a(b-d)+c(b+d),$$

and $2$ divides $x\bar x$ in $O$ exactly when $\sqrt2$ divides $x$.
lem-qc-denominator-exponent-well-defined:
## Statement

For every nonzero $z\in D$, the set
$\{k\in\mathbb Z:(\sqrt2)^kz\in O\}$ is nonempty and bounded below, hence
has a least integer.
lem-qc-dyadic-cyclotomic-conjugate-norm:
## Statement

Let $D=\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$ and
$D_+=\mathbb Z[\sqrt2,1/2]\subseteq\mathbb R$. For every $z\in D$, its
complex-conjugate norm satisfies $z^\dagger z\in D_+$. More precisely, if
$z=(a_0+a_1\omega+a_2\omega^2+a_3\omega^3)/2^r$ is its canonical encoding,
then
$$z^\dagger z=\frac{P+\sqrt2Q}{2^{2r}},\quad P=\sum_{j=0}^3a_j^2,\quad Q=a_0(a_1-a_3)+a_2(a_1+a_3).$$
lem-qc-dyadic-cyclotomic-unit-circle:
## Statement

If $z\in D$ and $z\bar z=1$, then $z=\omega^j$ for some $j\in\{0,1,\ldots,7\}$.
lem-qc-cyclotomic-euclidean-factorizatio:
## Statement

Put $R=\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$, $O=\mathbb Z[\omega]$, and
$\lambda=1+\sqrt2$. Both rings are norm-Euclidean domains and hence unique
factorization domains with effective gcd and associate tests. There is a
terminating finite-search algorithm factoring every nonzero element of $O$
into primes and a unit. The units of $R$ are exactly $\pm\lambda^j$
($j\in\mathbb Z$); a unit is positive at both real embeddings if and only
if it is a square of a unit of $R$. These assertions include effective square
root recovery. No polynomial runtime bound is asserted for finite-search
factorization.
lem-qc-cyclotomic-one-dimensional-grid-e:
## Statement

Put $\lambda=1+\sqrt2$. For bounded closed real intervals $I,J$, let $N$ count $\alpha\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$ with $\alpha\in I$, $\alpha^\bullet\in J$, and put $P=|I||J|$. There is an explicit finite proposal list containing every solution once, with constant work per proposal, of length $O(N+1)$. If both lengths are positive its length is $O(P+1)$, and $N\ge P/(4\lambda^3)$ when $P\ge4\lambda^3$. The list has constant-size random-access data. Empty intervals give empty lists; singleton intervals are also allowed. Floor operations are specified as integer-part operations, and their comparison cost is charged separately, rather than assumed constant.
lem-qc-paired-ellipse-grid-uprighting:
## Statement

Let $E,F$ be ellipses in $\mathbb R^2$, specified by their centers and positive definite symmetric matrices. Normalize their matrices separately to determinant one, obtaining $D_0,\Delta_0$. Suppose the eigenvalues of both normalized matrices lie in $[H^{-1},H]$, $H\ge2$. There is a constructive real linear map $G$ such that $G\mathbb Z[\omega]=\mathbb Z[\omega]$, $\det G=\pm1$, $(Gu)^\bullet=G^\bullet u^\bullet$, and both $G(E)$ and $G^\bullet(F)$ have area at least $1/6$ of their axis-aligned bounding-box area. It uses $O(\log H)$ matrix/arithmetic/logarithm/exponentiation operations and $O(\log H)$ integer-part operations. All real quantities to which integer parts are applied have magnitude $H^{O(1)}$, so implementing those parts by comparisons and binary search costs $O((\log H)^2)$ operations overall. The entries of $G,G^\bullet$ have magnitude $H^{O(1)}$.
def-qc-denominator-exponent:
## Definition

For nonzero $z\in D$, define
$\operatorname{sde}(z)=\min\{k\in\mathbb Z:(\sqrt2)^kz\in O\}$; exponents may
be negative. Set $\operatorname{sde}(0)=-\infty$. For a matrix $U$, the
denominator statistic used in the synthesis statements below is
$\operatorname{sde}(|U_{00}|^2)$, the exponent of the squared modulus of its
upper-left entry. The base regime in this convention is exponent at most $3$.
thm-qc-cyclotomic-norm-equation-decision:
## Statement

For every $\xi\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt2,1/2]$ there is a terminating exact
algorithm deciding whether $t^\dagger t=\xi$ has a solution
$t\in D=\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$, and returning such a solution when one
exists. A supplied prime factorization of the numerator of
$\xi^\bullet\xi$ is permissible but unnecessary for the finite-search
version below. No polynomial runtime bound is asserted.

More explicitly, reject a negative real embedding; handle $\xi=0$ by
$t=0$. Otherwise choose $r\ge0$ with $\eta=4^r\xi\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$
and factor $\eta$ into primes of $O=\mathbb Z[\omega]$. Group the prime
associate classes into orbits of complex conjugation. There is a solution
exactly when every conjugation-fixed class has even exponent. The
conjugation-paired classes have equal exponents automatically. Allocate half
of each fixed exponent, and the whole exponent to one representative of each
pair, to form $s$. Recover a real unit $v$ with
$v^2=\eta/(s^\dagger s)$; then $t=vs/2^r$ is an exact solution.
alg-qc-rz-efficient-scaled-grid-iterator:
## Definition

Inputs are $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and the unit vector $w=e^{-i\theta/2}$, in the ideal exact-real arithmetic/comparison model. Put $h=\varepsilon^2/2$ and
$$ A=\{u:|u|\le1,\ \operatorname{Re}(\bar w u)\ge1-h\},\qquad B=\{u:|u|\le1\}. $$
The outer ellipse $E$ has center $(1-h/2)w$, semiaxes $h$ in direction $w$ and $2\sqrt h$ perpendicular to $w$. Compute $G$ simultaneously uprighting $E,B$ by [[lem-qc-paired-ellipse-grid-uprighting]], including its balancing operations, with $H=4/\varepsilon$. Retain this map for every layer. All subsequent coordinates are exact. Square roots in line/ellipse intersections are positive real exponentiation, or equivalently their comparisons can use sign tests and squared inequalities. Integer parts are obtained by bounded binary search, with their comparison cost charged.

Process denominator layers $k=0,1,\ldots$ in order. At $k=0$, solve the grid problem for $A,B$ in $\mathbb Z[\omega]$. At $k\ge1$, run three disjoint subproblems, indexed by $r\in\{1,\omega,1+\omega\}$: write
$$ u=(r+\sqrt2 v)/(\sqrt2)^k,\qquad v\in\mathbb Z[\omega], $$
and impose the corresponding affine constraints on $v,v^\bullet$. In each subproblem apply $G$ to $v$ and $G^\bullet$ to $v^\bullet$, and replace the constraints by their affine images. Their outer ellipses are translated/scaled copies of $G(E),G^\bullet(B)$. For each of the two lattice cosets $v'=\alpha+i\beta+s\omega$, $s=0,1$, translate both constraint sets appropriately, remembering that $\omega^\bullet=-\omega$. The unknowns $\alpha,\beta$ then lie in $\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$.

Construct a finite proposal domain for each resulting subproblem as follows. Let $I_x,I_y$ be the coordinate intervals of its first outer ellipse's bounding box, and $J_x,J_y$ those of its second; set $P_x=|I_x||J_x|$, $P_y=|I_y||J_y|$ and the fixed constant $T=4\lambda^3 64^2$, $\lambda=1+\sqrt2$.

- If both $P_x,P_y\ge T$, use the Cartesian product of the two one-dimensional proposal lists from [[lem-qc-cyclotomic-one-dimensional-grid-enumeration]]. Filter each proposal by the original exact cap and disk inequalities after inverse transformations.
- Otherwise take a coordinate with product less than $T$, enumerate and filter its one-dimensional list completely, and retain its finitely many actual coordinate solutions. For each, compute the two exact remaining-coordinate slice intervals of the transformed cap and disk. Each is the intersection of a quadratic interval and a linear half-line; compute it by the quadratic formula and sign tests, declaring it empty when appropriate. Use the one-dimensional proposal list on these slice intervals, including its singleton rule, and test both original constraints. Before normalizing a positive first slice width $\delta$ with second width $\Delta$, if $\delta<1/(\Delta+1)$, enlarge that first interval concentrically to width $1/(\Delta+1)$ and retain the original slice inequalities as filters; its new length product is at most one. For singleton second intervals first use the singleton enlargement of the one-dimensional lemma. This padding prevents arbitrarily small slice widths from causing an unbounded unit-rescaling exponent.

Each component is a Cartesian index range or one of finitely many one-dimensional ranges. Keep their lengths and prefix sums, so a domain index specifies one proposal without materializing a long list. Map a retained point back to $u$. Maintain a set of already emitted exact coefficient tuples for the current layer.

To stream the layer, interleave a random proposal attempt with the next index of an exhaustive sequential scan. For domain size $M>0$, a random attempt draws $q=\lceil\log_2 M\rceil$ unbiased bits and treats them as an integer $z$. If $z<M$, visit proposal $z$; otherwise omit the random visit on this iteration. In either case advance the exhaustive scan by one index. Thus accepted random visits are uniform and a random attempt is accepted with probability at least $1/2$, while rejection cannot block the exhaustive scan. At each visit emit its retained $u$ if not already emitted. Stop the layer once the sequential scan finishes, then discard its emitted set and advance to $k+1$. For an empty proposal domain advance immediately. This is a randomized within-layer order with deterministic finite-layer completion; it promises no lexicographic tie order. The enumeration and its complexity are established in [[thm-qc-rz-efficient-scaled-grid-enumeration]].
lem-qc-cyclotomic-scaled-grid-finiteness:
## Statement

Let $\bullet$ be the automorphism of $K=\mathbb Q(\omega)$ defined in
[[def-qc-cyclotomic-bullet-automorphism]], so $\omega^\bullet=-\omega=\omega^5$,
and let $u\in D\setminus\{0\}$ satisfy
$|u|\le1$ and $|u^\bullet|\le1$. Then $k=\operatorname{sde}(u)\ge0$. If
$a=(\sqrt2)^ku=a_0+a_1\omega+a_2\omega^2+a_3\omega^3$, then

$$|a_j|\le2^{k/2}\quad(0\le j\le3).$$

Thus for each fixed $k$ only finitely many coefficient vectors can occur; the
integer search may be restricted to
$|a_j|\le\lfloor2^{k/2}\rfloor$.
lem-qc-squared-entry-denominator-bound:
## Statement

For nonzero $z\in D$, write $s=\operatorname{sde}(z)$. There is
$m\in\{0,1\}$ such that
$\operatorname{sde}(|z|^2)=2s-m$. In particular, if
$\operatorname{sde}(|z|^2)\le3$, then $\operatorname{sde}(z)\le2$.
cor-qc-cyclotomic-prime-norm-solvability:
## Statement

Let $\xi\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt2,1/2]$ be positive at both real embeddings.
If $\xi^\bullet\xi=p/2^\ell$ with $\ell\ge0$ and a rational prime
$p\equiv1\pmod8$, then $t^\dagger t=\xi$ has a solution in
$\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$. The complete finite-time norm solver returns a
solution on every such input. The same conclusion holds when
$\xi^\bullet\xi=1/2^\ell$. No runtime bound is implied.
thm-qc-factored-cyclotomic-norm-equation:
## Statement

Put $R=\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$, $O=\mathbb Z[\omega]$, and $D=O[1/2]$, with $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$. Given $\xi\in R[1/2]$ and a valid complete rational-prime factorization of the nonzero numerator $n$ in the reduced fraction $\xi^\bullet\xi=n/2^\ell$, there is an exact randomized algorithm returning $t\in D$ with $t^\dagger t=\xi$, or correctly reporting that no such $t$ exists. Zero input requires no factorization. The algorithm terminates almost surely and has expected bit cost polynomial in the total binary length $L$ of the explicitly encoded rational coefficients of $\xi$ and the supplied factorization. Denominators are ordinary binary integers, not compressed exponent encodings. The algorithm does not compute or verify rational primality of the promised prime factors.

In particular, suppose $0\le\xi,\xi^\bullet\le1$, and $k$ is the least nonnegative integer with $(\sqrt2)^k\xi\in R$. Given the factorization of $n$, the expected cost, including exact solution recovery or a correct negative answer, is polynomial in $k+1$ when $\xi$ is supplied in reduced coefficient form. For a grid candidate $u\in D$ with least $\sqrt2$-denominator exponent $h$, its residual $\xi=1-u^\dagger u$ has least exponent at most $2h$. Under the same embedding bounds, $n\le4^h$ and the residual solver has expected cost polynomial in $h+1$. The unrestricted cost includes the bit length of the coefficients, rather than depending on $\log n$ alone.

For the stated grid residual with $n$ prime, or $n\in\{0,1\}$, a concrete schoolbook implementation of this algorithm has expected bit cost at most $P(h)=2^{200}(h+1)^{20}$. This explicit bound includes input reading in reduced coefficient form and exact verification of a returned solution. Bit cost counts Boolean operations and bit reads/writes on binary arrays; multi-bit arithmetic is performed by the schoolbook loops detailed below. It gives a numerical cap for interrupted attempts; it makes no correctness or termination assertion about calling prime-specific branches with a composite integer falsely presented as prime.
lem-qc-rz-scaled-grid-growth:
## Statement

Let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and let $u_1,u_2,\ldots$ be the distinct points in
$\mathcal G=\{u\in D:|u|,|u^\bullet|\le1,\ \operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta/2}u)\ge1-\varepsilon^2/2\}$,
ordered by nondecreasing least denominator exponent $k_j$.
Put $K=\lceil\log_2(512/\varepsilon^2)\rceil$. Then this sequence is infinite,
$k_2\le K$, and
$$k_j\le k_2+2\lceil\log_2 j\rceil\qquad(j\ge1).$$
More generally, if two bounded convex plane regions $A,B$ contain disks of
radii $r,R>0$, the simultaneous grid
$\{u\in(\sqrt2)^{-k}O:u\in A,\ u^\bullet\in B\}$ has at least two points
whenever $2^k rR\ge128$.
lem-qc-rz-candidate-norm-integer:
## Statement

Let $u\in D$ satisfy $|u|,|u^\bullet|\le1$, put
$\xi=1-u^\dagger u$, and write $\xi^\bullet\xi=n/2^\ell$ with
$n\in\mathbb Z$ and least $\ell\ge0$. Then $n\ge0$, and either $n=0$ or
$n\equiv1\pmod8$. If $u\ne0$ has least square-root-of-two denominator
exponent $k$, then $n\le4^k$.
thm-qc-rz-efficient-scaled-grid-enumerat:
## Statement

The iterator [[alg-qc-rz-efficient-scaled-grid-iterator]] enumerates exactly once every $u\in\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$ satisfying $u\in A$, $u^\bullet\in B$, in increasing least $\sqrt2$ denominator exponent. Let $L=1+\log(1/\varepsilon)$. Its startup costs $O(L^2)$ ideal exact-real arithmetic/comparison operations. In a layer $k$ having $N$ solutions, its explicit proposal domain has size $M\le C(N+1)$ for an absolute constant $C$, without filtering already emitted lower-denominator points. Empty layers cost $\operatorname{poly}(k+L)$. For $1\le j\le N$, the expected work through its first $j$ distinct outputs is $O(j(1+\log j)\operatorname{poly}(k+L))$; the $r$th moment of that prefix work is $O_r(j^{2r}\operatorname{poly}(k+L)^r)$ for every fixed positive integer $r$. Complete-layer work is $O((N+1)\operatorname{poly}(k+L))$ in expectation. These are arithmetic bounds with random-bit generation charged, and do not assert bit-time bounds for unspecified real inputs or worst-case polynomial delay.
lem-qc-rz-prime-model-stopping-bounds:
## Statement

For the candidate sequence and exponents of
[[lem-qc-rz-scaled-grid-growth]], let $E_j$ be success events and $J=\min\{j\ge1:E_j\}$.
Suppose there are numbers $p_j\in[0,1]$ with $p_j\ge c/(k_j+1)$, for a constant $0<c\le1$
independent of the input, such that
$$\Pr(J>j)\le\prod_{i=1}^j(1-p_i)\qquad(j\ge1).$$
Independent success events of probabilities $p_j$ are a sufficient special
case; independence of the events is not otherwise required.
Then $J<\infty$ almost surely and, for every fixed positive integer $r$,
$$\mathbb E[J^r]=O((k_2+1)^r)=O((1+\log(1/\varepsilon))^r).$$
In particular $\mathbb E[J]=O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ and
$\mathbb E[\log_2J]=O(1+\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$.
The implied constants can depend on $c$ and $r$, but not on $\theta$ or
$\varepsilon$. For every fixed nonnegative integer $d$,
$\mathbb E[J(1+k_2+\log J)^d]$ is polynomially bounded in $1+k_2$.

This is the explicit quantitative probabilistic assumption needed when
Ross–Selinger Hypothesis 8.3 is used for a complexity claim. It is a conditional
model, not an assertion of independence for a deterministic input sequence.
def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library:
## Definition

Let $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$. The one-qubit generators and exact matrices in the
ordered computational basis are

$$H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\omega\end{pmatrix},\qquad T^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\omega^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$

On basis vectors, $H|q\rangle=(|0\rangle+(-1)^q|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and
$T^k|q\rangle=\omega^{kq}|q\rangle$ for $q\in\{0,1\}$.

Write $S=T^2=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ and
$Z=T^4=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Pauli $X,Y,Z$ are as in
[[def-qc-pauli-matrices]]. On two ordered wires,
$\operatorname{CNOT}|a,b\rangle=|a,b\mathbin\oplus a\rangle$; the first wire
is control and the second target. A circuit is a finite chronological word of
these gates at stated wire positions; its matrix is the product with later
gates on the left. No extra wire or controlled-$T$ operation is implicit.

The scalar phase $\omega I$ is an allowed Clifford phase in the one-qubit
matrix-word convention. Its scalar factor is retained in exact matrix products;
the convention that an overall scalar does not affect a resource count is
stated separately from matrix equality. It does not grant a controlled-$T$
operation or allow a scalar on a target wire to be discarded under control.

The exact one-qubit H/T algebra is generated by $H,T,T^\dagger$; $S$ and $Z$
are aliases for the displayed powers. The distinction between exact matrix
equality and [[def-qc-global-phase-equivalence|global-phase equivalence]] is
maintained. Resource costs are supplied by
[[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]] and remain separate from this matrix
definition.
alg-qc-controlled-t-clean-ancilla-circui:
## Definition

Input two data bits $a,b$ and a third clean work bit $t=0$. On the ordered
register $(a,b,t)$, apply the following chronological word:

1. $H_t$.
2. $\operatorname{CNOT}_{b,t},T_t^\dagger,\operatorname{CNOT}_{a,t},T_t,
   \operatorname{CNOT}_{b,t},T_t^\dagger,\operatorname{CNOT}_{a,t}$.
3. $T_b,T_t,H_t$.
4. $\operatorname{CNOT}_{a,b},T_a,T_b^\dagger,\operatorname{CNOT}_{a,b}$.
5. Apply the same 15-gate word again.

The 15-gate word in steps 1–4 is the specified three-wire block. The output
is the complete three-wire circuit, with no implicit fourth wire.
def-qc-ancilla-free-rz-approximation-pro:
## Definition

For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ set
$R_z(\theta)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{-i\theta/2},e^{i\theta/2})$. Given
$0<\varepsilon<1/2$, the on-the-nose ancilla-free approximation problem is to
find a finite one-qubit Clifford+T word $U$ such that

$$\|R_z(\theta)-U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon,$$

and minimize the number of occurrences of $T$ or $T^\dagger$; the $T$-count
of a word is this integer. An overall scalar Clifford phase $\omega^j I$,
viewed under [[def-qc-global-phase-equivalence]], is free in the resource
count but remains part of the exact matrix used in the displayed norm
inequality. Thus changing the representative can change feasibility even
when it leaves T-count unchanged. No workspace wire is
permitted. The operator norm is the finite-dimensional norm from
[[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].

This defines a mathematical optimization problem for exact real inputs
$(\theta,\varepsilon)$. It does not specify a bit representation or assert a
Turing algorithm for arbitrary real input.
lem-qc-clifford-t-determinant-phase:
## Statement

Every exact one-qubit Clifford+T matrix word, including a free scalar
Clifford phase $\omega^j I$, has determinant in
$\{\omega^k:k\in\mathbb Z\}$.
lem-qc-clifford-t-entry-ring:
## Statement

Every finite circuit on $n$ ordered wires using only the matrices in
[[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]] has all matrix entries in $D$.
lem-qc-hadamard-reduced-word-denominator:
## Statement

Use $G=\{H,T,T^\dagger,S,S^\dagger,X,Y,Z\}$ and allow scalar phases $\omega^qI$. Only $H$ contributes to the H count; only $T,T^\dagger$ contribute to the T count. Every word can be rewritten, with its exact scalar retained, as

$$\omega^q T^a H T^{b_1}H\cdots H T^{b_{h-1}}H T^c X^e,$$

where all $b_i$ are odd, exponents are read modulo $8$, and $e\in\{0,1\}$. For $h=0$ interpret this as $\omega^qT^aX^e$. The rewriting never increases either resource count. Each odd power uses one T gate and even powers use none. A reduced word with $h\ge2$ has $\operatorname{sde}(|U_{00}|^2)=h+1$; with $h=1$ the exponent is $2$, and with $h=0$ the squared entry is $0$ or $1$. Consequently reduced words minimize H count among all words for the same matrix up to global phase.
alg-qc-cyclotomic-scaled-grid-and-norm-s:
## Definition

Fix $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$ and $D=\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$. Use the automorphism
$\bullet$ from [[def-qc-cyclotomic-bullet-automorphism]], which sends
$\omega$ to $-\omega=\omega^5$ and fixes $i$. Let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and
$\theta\in\mathbb R$. The scaled grid for this input is

$$\mathcal G(\theta,\varepsilon)=\{u\in D:\ |u|\le1,\ |u^\bullet|\le1,\ \operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta/2}u)\ge1-\varepsilon^2/2\}.$$

The default iterator is [[alg-qc-rz-efficient-scaled-grid-iterator]], with
$w=e^{-i\theta/2}$. It emits every candidate once in increasing least
$k=\operatorname{sde}(u)$, with randomized order within each layer and
finite layer completion for every random-bit sequence. Its expected prefix
cost and all fixed prefix moments are proved in
[[thm-qc-rz-efficient-scaled-grid-enumeration]].

A complete finite-search alternative uses lexicographic power-basis
coefficients within each layer. For each $k\ge0$, write
$u=(a_0+a_1\omega+a_2\omega^2+a_3\omega^3)/(\sqrt2)^k$ with least exponent
$k$; the finite coefficient bound is
$|a_j|\le\lfloor2^{k/2}\rfloor$, proved in
[[lem-qc-cyclotomic-scaled-grid-finiteness]]. Test the three displayed
conditions exactly. This defines a finite candidate list for each $k$.

For a candidate $u$, put
$\xi=1-u^\dagger u=1-|u|^2\in D_+=\mathbb Z[\sqrt2,1/2]$, using
[[lem-qc-dyadic-cyclotomic-conjugate-norm]]. For scalars, $z^\dagger=\bar z$.
Write
$\xi^\bullet\xi=n/2^\ell$ with $n\in\mathbb Z$ and least $\ell\ge0$; compute
it by writing $\xi=a+b\sqrt2$ with $a,b\in\mathbb Z[1/2]$ and multiplying
$(a-b\sqrt2)(a+b\sqrt2)=a^2-2b^2$. The two disk conditions give
$\xi,\xi^\bullet\ge0$, so $n\ge0$; if $\xi\ne0$, injectivity of $\bullet$
gives $n>0$.
The complete norm-equation subprocedure receives $\xi$ and, if $n\ne0$, a prime
factorization of $n$. It must decide whether some $t\in D$ satisfies
$t^\dagger t=\xi$, return an exact such $t$ if one exists, and otherwise return
`NO_SOLUTION`. If $\xi=0$, it returns $t=0$. A bounded factorization attempt
may return `FACTOR_TIMEOUT`; that result skips this candidate and is not a
proof of `NO_SOLUTION`.

### Factored norm-equation subprocedure

When the supplied integer factorization is available, use the efficient
construction in [[thm-qc-factored-cyclotomic-norm-equation-efficient]].
Clear the denominator by $\eta=4^r\xi$, taking the least nonnegative
$r$ for which $\eta\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$. For each rational prime in its
known norm factorization, recover its real prime generators using
$\gcd(p,\sqrt2-b)$ when $b^2=2\pmod p$ exists, and otherwise retain
$p$. Split these into cyclotomic prime generators by the displayed modular
roots of $-1$ or $-2$ and cyclotomic gcds; retain the inert generators and
include $\delta=1+\omega$ over $2$. Recover the exponents in
$\eta$ by exact division, allocate them under complex conjugation as below,
and recover the real unit by multiplying by $1+\sqrt2$ or its inverse
until its positive embedding lies in $[1,1+\sqrt2)$.
The cited construction specifies all residue-class branches and its
randomized modular square-root subroutine; balance gcd remainders by real
units as there. It returns an exact solution or `NO_SOLUTION` and has
expected polynomial bit cost in the explicit algebraic input size. For a
grid candidate of exponent $k$, this is polynomial in $k+1$.

### Calibrated bounded prime attempts

In bounded mode no prime recognition oracle is used. For candidate exponent
$k$, use the fixed calibrated polynomial
$$P(k)=2^{200}(k+1)^{20}$$
from [[thm-qc-factored-cyclotomic-norm-equation-efficient]]. If $n=0$,
return $t=0$. If $n=1$, run the complete efficient construction with the
empty odd-prime factor list; its remaining powers of two are known.

For $n>1$, execute the factored construction prospectively, using the
single factor hint $n^1$, for at most $2P(k)$ of its elementary binary
operations. This is an attempt, not a claim that $n$ is prime. Instrument
all loops, including random sampling, with this counter. Guard every partial
operation: check divisors for zero and obtain modular inverses by the
integer extended Euclidean algorithm, aborting if the gcd is not one.
Impossible order/root searches, malformed outputs, negative solver outcomes,
failed inverses, and work-cap interruptions all end the attempt with
`FACTOR_TIMEOUT`, never with a claim of `NO_SOLUTION`.

Before accepting any prospective output, reduce its rational power-basis
coefficients and check $t^\dagger t=\xi$ exactly. Accept only when that
equality holds; otherwise return `FACTOR_TIMEOUT`. Watchdog, guard and final
certificate costs are charged; they are polynomial in $k+1+P(k)$ even on
composite inputs. The solver-work counter bounds every intermediate bit
string by its input length plus $2P(k)$, so certification cannot hide an
unbounded output cost. Use fresh independent random bits at each candidate.

An optional extra factoring attempt may be given a declared budget $Q(k)$
after this prime attempt fails (default $Q=0$). Any suggested factor list is
used only for another guarded, capped prospective norm call, with total
additional work bounded by $Q(k)$. Again accept only an exact norm
certificate and otherwise skip. In particular an uncertified prime hint or
negative result is never used as proof of unsolvability. For the polynomial
runtime guarantee choose a polynomial $Q$; any fixed finite budget is a
special case. Complete oracle mode instead supplies a valid full
factorization and runs the complete efficient solver without this cap.

### Complete finite-search alternative

Use the complete terminating construction of
[[thm-qc-cyclotomic-norm-equation-decision]]. Explicitly, after the zero
case choose the least integer $r\ge0$ clearing the coefficient denominators so that
$\eta=4^r\xi\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$. Factor $\eta$ in
$O=\mathbb Z[\omega]$ by the finite divisor search in
[[lem-qc-cyclotomic-euclidean-factorization-and-units]]. Group the prime
associate classes under $\dagger$. If any fixed class has odd exponent,
return `NO_SOLUTION`. Otherwise form $s$ by allocating half each fixed
exponent, and all of the common exponent to one class from each conjugate
pair. Compute the positive real unit $e=\eta/(s^\dagger s)$, recover
$v\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]$ with $v^2=e$ by the unit construction, and return
$t=vs/2^r$. Every computation here uses exact power-basis arithmetic.

The supplied integer factorization is retained as an admissible input for
implementations using rational-prime splitting. The finite-search mode above
does not need it and has no asserted polynomial runtime. A factorization
timeout is a separate optional candidate-skipping policy, as specified above;
it never changes the complete subprocedure's `NO_SOLUTION` criterion.

### Comparison contract

The grid comparisons involve the supplied real parameters $\theta$ and
$\varepsilon$. Their exact comparison interface is part of the outer
real-input contract. It is independent of the algebraic norm solver, whose
sign, equality, divisibility and associate tests are all exact and terminating.
lem-qc-clifford-t-determinant-one-approx:
## Statement

Let $G$ be the group of exact one-qubit Clifford+T matrix words, and let
$SU(2)=\{U\in U(2):\det U=1\}$. For every $R\in SU(2)$ and every
$\varepsilon>0$, some $W\in G$ satisfies $\det W=1$ and
$\|R-W\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\varepsilon$.
lem-qc-rz-epsilon-region-equivalence:
## Statement

Let $\theta\in\mathbb R$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and
$$U=\begin{pmatrix}u&-\bar t\\t&\bar u\end{pmatrix}\in SU(2).$$
Then
$$\|R_z(\theta)-U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta/2}u)\ge1-\varepsilon^2/2.$$
lem-qc-single-qubit-ring-unitary-form:
## Statement

If $U=\begin{pmatrix}u&b\\v&d\end{pmatrix}$ is a $2\times2$ unitary with
entries in $D$, then for some $j\in\{0,\ldots,7\}$,

$$U=\begin{pmatrix}u&-\omega^j\bar v\\v&\omega^j\bar u\end{pmatrix},\qquad |u|^2+|v|^2=1.$$
prop-qc-controlled-t-clean-ancilla-corre:
## Statement

The procedure of [[alg-qc-controlled-t-clean-ancilla-circuit]] acts on every
computational basis input $|a,b,0\rangle$ as
$|a,b,0\rangle\mapsto\omega^{ab}|a,b,0\rangle$. Consequently it implements
$C(T)$ on the two data bits and returns the clean ancilla to $|0\rangle$,
also when the data is entangled with any finite-dimensional reference register.
thm-qc-controlled-t-two-qubit-obstructio:
## Statement

The two-qubit controlled-$T$ matrix
$C(T)=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,\omega)$ cannot be implemented exactly, or
up to a scalar global phase, by a circuit on exactly two wires using only
one-qubit Clifford+T gates and CNOT. The assertion concerns no workspace wire;
it does not rule out implementations with an explicit ancilla.
thm-qc-rz-synthesis-up-to-phase:
## Statement

For $R=R_z(\theta)$ and a one-qubit Clifford+T operator $U$, if
$\|R-\lambda U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon$ for some unit scalar $\lambda$,
then the same projective T-count has a representative whose phase parameter
is one of $1$ or $e^{i\pi/8}$. The exact representative in the operator-norm
constraint remains explicit in the pair $(\lambda,U)$. Thus the up-to-phase
search need only compare the two scaled candidate problems. If such a
phase-equivalent operator is placed
under a control, its phase must be restored as a relative phase:

$$C(\lambda U)=\bigl(\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda)\otimes I\bigr)C(U).$$
lem-qc-clifford-t-denominator-descent-an:
## Statement

Let $(u,v)^T$ be a unit vector with entries in $D$, and put
$s=\operatorname{sde}(|u|^2)$. If $s>3$, then some $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ has

$$\operatorname{sde}\!\left(\left|\frac{u+\omega^{-k}v}{\sqrt2}\right|^2\right)=s-1.$$

Moreover, every such unit column with $s\le3$ is prepared exactly from
$|0\rangle$ by a word in $H,T,T^\dagger$. A complete coefficient-and-word
table for the finite base set is recorded at
`research/quantum-computing-algorithms-60-2026-10-15-batch-13-finite-certificates.json`.
lem-qc-rz-scaled-grid-norm-solution-exis:
## Statement

For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, there are $u,t\in D$
such that
$$|u|\le1,\qquad |u^\bullet|\le1,\qquad \operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta/2}u)\ge1-\varepsilon^2/2,\qquad t^\dagger t=1-u^\dagger u.$$
Thus the scaled grid has at least one candidate whose norm equation is
solvable.
lem-qc-rz-determinant-one-reduction:
## Statement

Set $c=|1-e^{i\pi/8}|$. If $0<\varepsilon<c$, every exact one-qubit
Clifford+T matrix $V$ with $\|R_z(\theta)-V\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon$
has determinant one. If $\varepsilon\ge c$, there is a determinant-one
Clifford matrix of T-count zero meeting this error bound. Consequently,
for every positive precision the minimum T-count over all feasible matrices
is attained among determinant-one matrices.
lem-qc-capped-prime-norm-attempt-success:
## Statement

Let $u$ be a grid candidate of least denominator exponent $k$, and put
$\xi=1-u^\dagger u$, $\xi^\bullet\xi=n/2^\ell$ in reduced form.
Let $P(k)=2^{200}(k+1)^{20}$ be the calibrated prime-input binary-work
bound of [[thm-qc-factored-cyclotomic-norm-equation-efficient]]. The capped prime-attempt procedure in
[[alg-qc-cyclotomic-scaled-grid-and-norm-solver]], with solver budget
$2\lceil P(k)\rceil$, has the following properties:

- Every accepted output is an exact solution $t^\dagger t=\xi$.
- On every input its work is polynomial in $k+1$, including the final exact
  verification, with no primality promise on $n$.
- When $n$ is prime, its success probability is at least $1/2$. When
  $n\in\{0,1\}$, the explicitly complete zero/unit branches succeed.

For a candidate stream with exponent profile $k_j$, suppose its arithmetic
data are given an idealized stochastic model in which the indicators $I_j$
of prime or zero/unit norm numerators are independent, with
$p_j=\Pr(I_j=1)\ge c/(k_j+1)$. Draw fresh independent solver bits,
independently of all arithmetic data. If $J$ is the first successful call,
then
$$\Pr(J>j)\le\prod_{i=1}^j(1-p_i/2)\le\prod_{i=1}^j\left(1-\frac{c}{2(k_i+1)}\right).$$
Thus these attempts have the same stopping-tail bound as independent events
with probabilities $c/(2(k_j+1))$. Independence of the actual successful-call
events is not asserted or needed. This last assertion concerns the explicit
stochastic model; the numerators of an actual fixed input have fixed
primality, while the first three assertions above hold for each such input.
thm-qc-single-qubit-exact-clifford-t-cha:
## Statement

A matrix $U\in U(2)$ is exactly the matrix of a finite one-qubit Clifford+T
word if and only if all four entries of $U$ lie in $D$. This is a
single-qubit statement; no multi-qubit exact ring characterization is
asserted.
alg-qc-exact-single-qubit-clifford-t-syn:
## Definition

Input a $2\times2$ matrix $U$ as four canonical elements of $D$. Perform the
following exact procedure.

1. Test $U^*U=I$ by rational coefficient arithmetic. If it fails, return
   `INVALID`.
2. Set $M=U$ and an empty list $K$. While
   $s=\operatorname{sde}(|M_{00}|^2)>3$, test $k=0,1,2,3$ in that order and
   choose the first for which
$\operatorname{sde}(|(HT^{-k}M)_{00}|^2)=s-1$. Append $k$ to $K$ and replace
$M$ by $HT^{-k}M$.
3. Look up the first column of $M$ in the complete base-column table at
   `research/quantum-computing-algorithms-60-2026-10-15-batch-13-finite-certificates.json`.
   Let $W_0$ be its stored H/T preparation word. Compute
   $W_0^*M=\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda)$ exactly and find $j\in\{0,\ldots,7\}$
   with $\lambda=\omega^j$.
4. If $K=(k_1,\ldots,k_r)$ in reduction order, form the exact matrix-word
factorization
$$U=(T^{k_1}H)\cdots(T^{k_r}H)W_0T^j.$$
For the chronological output, emit $T^j$ first, then the stored chronological
gate list for $W_0$, then for $i=r,r-1,\ldots,1$ emit $H$ followed by
$T^{k_i}$. The QC09 semantics put later gates on the left, so this list has the
displayed matrix product.
5. Reduce this word by the exact stack rewriting in
   [[lem-qc-hadamard-reduced-word-denominators]]: move Pauli $X$ factors to
   the right, combine diagonal powers modulo eight, and replace each
   $HT^{2r}H$ by its zero- or one-H Clifford expression until all interior
   diagonal powers are odd. Retain the scalar phase $\omega^qI$ produced by
   these identities in the exact output. Emit even powers as $S,Z$ factors
   and odd powers as one $T$ or $T^\dagger$ with free $S,Z$ factors, then
   return the reduced factors in reverse order as the chronological list.

The denominator descent and table completeness are the mathematical
properties in [[lem-qc-clifford-t-denominator-descent-and-base]] and
[[thm-qc-single-qubit-exact-clifford-t-characterization]]. The finite lookup
table uses exact rational coefficients; no numerical equality tolerance is
used.
alg-qc-rz-clifford-t-approximation:
## Definition

Input exact reals $\theta$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, an exact-real comparison
capability for the grid inequalities, and either an integer-factorization
oracle or bounded mode with a declared additional factor-attempt budget
$Q(k)\ge0$ (default zero); a fixed finite budget is allowed. No bit encoding for
arbitrary reals is implicit. Use an independent random stream for the grid
iterator and fresh independent streams for each randomized norm call; the
candidate order depends only on the grid stream, not on norm-call outcomes.

1. Enumerate $u$ from
   [[alg-qc-cyclotomic-scaled-grid-and-norm-solver]] in increasing denominator
   exponent. For each candidate, compute $\xi=1-|u|^2$. In oracle mode
   obtain the complete integer factorization and invoke the efficient exact
   norm subprocedure; the finite-search complete solver is an alternative.
   In bounded mode use the calibrated capped prime attempt and its optional
   budgeted extra factoring attempt, accepting only an exact certificate.
2. If it returns `FACTOR_TIMEOUT` or `NO_SOLUTION`, continue to the next
   candidate. For each returned $t$ with $t^*t=\xi$, form
   $U=\begin{pmatrix}u&-\bar t\\t&\bar u\end{pmatrix}$ and
   $U'=TUT^\dagger$.
3. Run [[alg-qc-exact-single-qubit-clifford-t-synthesis]] on both matrices.
   Return the word with smaller exact T-count; break ties by lexicographic
   gate word. If a finite total candidate budget is supplied and is exhausted
   first, return `TIMEOUT`.

The exact grid-to-error equivalence is proved in
[[lem-qc-rz-epsilon-region-equivalence]]. The unbounded factoring-oracle mode
uses the complete efficient solver from the norm procedure, or the finite
alternative [[thm-qc-cyclotomic-norm-equation-decision]]. Successful
termination (almost surely for the randomized efficient mode) under the stated
terminating exact-real comparisons is proved in
[[thm-qc-rz-approximation-correct-on-termination]]. A finite-budget call can
return `TIMEOUT`. The complete finite-search norm mode gives no polynomial
arithmetic-time guarantee.
thm-qc-exact-clifford-t-synthesis-optima:
## Statement

Use $G=\{H,T,T^\dagger,S,S^\dagger,X,Y,Z\}$, with scalar phase ignored. Count each $H$ as one Hadamard and each $T$ or $T^\dagger$ as one T gate; $S,S^\dagger,X,Y,Z$ have zero H/T count. Let $h(U)$ and $t(U)$ be the separate minima. For $U\in M_2(D)$ unitary with $n=\operatorname{sde}(|U_{00}|^2)\ge4$, the exact synthesis algorithm, including its final reduced-word pass, attains both minima and

$$h(U)=n-1,\qquad t(U)=h(U)+1-(\ell\bmod2)-(j\bmod2),$$

where $\ell,j$ are any integers satisfying $h(HT^\ell UT^jH)=h(U)+2$. Such integers exist. Equivalently, if the reduced word has endpoint diagonal exponents $a,c$, then $t(U)=h(U)-1+(a\bmod2)+(c\bmod2)$. With canonical binary coefficient encoding the algorithm uses $O(n_{\rm opt}+1)$ ring operations and $O((n_{\rm opt}+1)^2)$ bit operations, where $n_{\rm opt}$ is the minimum total H/T count.

More generally, every reduced word with $h\ge1$ Hadamard gates and
endpoint diagonal exponents $a,c$ is T-optimal, with
$t=h-1+(a\bmod2)+(c\bmod2)$, including the $h=1,2$ cases.
thm-qc-exact-single-qubit-synthesis-corr:
## Statement

For every unitary $U\in M_2(D)$, the procedure in
[[alg-qc-exact-single-qubit-clifford-t-synthesis]] terminates and returns a
finite one-qubit Clifford+T word whose exact matrix is $U$.
thm-qc-rz-approximation-correct-on-termi:
## Statement

For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, any run of
[[alg-qc-rz-clifford-t-approximation]] that returns after its norm solver has
returned only exact solutions and its exact compiler has returned the
requested matrices satisfies
$\|R_z(\theta)-W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon$. Moreover, if the scaled-grid
enumeration is unbounded, the complete finite-search norm mode is used with a factoring
oracle, and every required exact-real comparison terminates, then the
procedure terminates for every such input. With the efficient factored norm
mode and independent random bits, oracle mode instead terminates with
probability one under the same terminating-comparison assumption.
lem-qc-su-two-denominator-t-count:
## Statement

Let $U=\begin{pmatrix}u&-\bar t\\t&\bar u\end{pmatrix}\in SU(2)$ with $u,t\in D$. Let $k$ be the least nonnegative integer such that $(\sqrt2)^ku,(\sqrt2)^kt\in O$. Count T gates over $G=\{H,T,T^\dagger,S,S^\dagger,X,Y,Z\}$ up to global phase. If $k>0$, each of $U$ and $TUT^\dagger$ has optimal T count in $\{2k-2,2k\}$, and

$$\min\{t(U),t(TUT^\dagger)\}=\max\{0,2k-2\}.$$

If $k=0$, both counts are zero. If $u,t$ are nonzero and $k>0$, their individual least exponents both equal $k$.
thm-qc-rz-clifford-t-tcount:
## Statement

For the ancilla-free, on-the-nose $R_z(\theta)$ problem with
$0<\varepsilon<1/2$, the Ross–Selinger grid/norm procedure has the following
source guarantees, with its exact-real comparison and norm-solver assumptions.

1. With a factoring oracle and a complete factorization-based solver for
   $t^*t=\xi$, the first successful candidate yields a circuit of minimum
   T-count among all one-qubit Clifford+T circuits satisfying the operator
   norm bound.
2. In bounded-factorization mode, under Ross–Selinger Hypothesis 8.3,
   interpreted quantitatively as [A1] below, if $m$ is the returned T-count
   and $m''$ is the second-smallest T-count among non-equivalent feasible
   solutions, then the expected number of non-equivalent feasible solutions
   of T-count strictly below $m$ is $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$, and
   $\mathbb E[m]\le m''+O(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$ as $\varepsilon\to0$.
3. With the efficient iterator and calibrated capped-prime implementation
   specified below,
   the expected arithmetic-operation time is
   $O(\operatorname{polylog}(1/\varepsilon))$. This is not a
   bit-time bound for arbitrary unencoded real inputs.

Two determinant-one solutions are equivalent when their upper-left entries
$u$ agree; the T-count of a class is the least count attained in that class.
The near-optimality assertion concerns the unbounded candidate stream, without
a finite total candidate budget. The source's notation
$\mathbb E[m]=m''+O(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$ is used here only in the upper
bound sense proved in its Proposition 8.8; no lower bound relative to the
second-best class is asserted.
